transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I came because... well, I feel a little awful even admitting this, because I don't want to sound ungrateful or make a fuss. But lately, even when my wonderful children come to sit with me, or... or when the sun is shining right on my garden, I just feel... flat inside. Is that the right way to describe it? 

It's just, it's like the part of me that could be glad, or comforted by those things, just sort of... shut off. I know I should feel happy, and I try so hard to be pleasant for them, I really do. Am I explaining that alright for you?
Can you tell me if this feeling of being flat or shut off happens most days, and if it tends to last throughout the day, even when things around you are positive or pleasant?

Well, I suppose... yes, it does seem to be most days. I hate to say it, because I really am so blessed to have my family and my little home. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, you know? 

But yes, even when they bring me a nice cup of tea or show me a lovely drawing the grandchildren made, I just... I smile and say thank you, because I know it's a beautiful thing, but the feeling inside just doesn't quite match. It stays like that pretty much all day. I try to shake it off, I really do. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, even activities that you normally find pleasurable or meaningful?

Oh, I wouldn't say that... I mean, I still make sure to tend to my indoor plants, and I always watch my evening programs. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around moping all day, because I'm really not! 

I still find those things pleasant, I think. I haven't really noticed a change in... in liking them, exactly. It's just that quiet, flat feeling underneath it all, like I mentioned before. But I still keep busy with my little hobbies and try to make the best of it. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know.

Looking back at the last few weeks, have you found that activities you used to enjoy, like tending to your plants or watching your favorite shows, don’t bring you the same sense of pleasure or satisfaction they used to?

Well, um... I know you just asked about that, and I'm sorry if I didn't explain it well the first time. I really don't want to be difficult. 

I think... I think I still get some satisfaction from them. Like, when I water my African violets and see a new little bloom, I do think, "Oh, isn't that nice." I really do. I don't think I've stopped enjoying them entirely. I try very hard to focus on those good little moments, you know? 

So, I wouldn't say the pleasure is gone. It's just... maybe just a little quieter than it used to be? Because of that flat feeling I was talking about. But I'm still doing them, and I still like them. Does that... does that answer your question better? I'm so sorry if I'm not being clear enough.
Even if you still do your usual activities like tending to your plants or watching your shows, have you found that you look forward to them less or feel less interested in them than before?

Oh, goodness, you're being so thorough, and I appreciate that, I really do. I don't mean to make you go over the same ground. 

Um... I suppose... no, I don't think I'm less interested. I still make sure I'm settled in my chair right at seven for my programs, just like always. I wouldn't want to miss them. And my plants, well, they need me, don't they? I couldn't just lose interest in them. 

I think I still look forward to things just fine. I try to keep a positive attitude about my day, you see. I hope I'm being helpful... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are. I'm doing my best to keep up with everything, truly I am. Is that what you were asking?
Even though you still do your usual activities, have you noticed that you have to push yourself more to get started or stay involved with them compared to before?

Oh, I... I'm so sorry, I feel like you're trying to get at something and I'm just not giving you the right answer. I don't want to be frustrating for you. 

But no, I wouldn't say I have to push myself. I mean, it's just what I do, isn't it? The plants need watering, the shows come on... it's just my routine. I don't really have to force myself to do them. I just get up and do what needs doing, like I always have. I try to be very disciplined about my day, you see. I don't want to be one of those people who just lets everything go. 

I really hope I'm being helpful. I'm trying my best to answer you properly, I promise. Am I... am I giving you what you need?
Even though you're still doing your usual activities, do you find that you don't care about them as much as you used to, even just a little bit?

Oh, dear... I feel like I'm making this so difficult for you, and I really don't mean to. You're being so patient with me. 

Um... no, I don't think I care about them any less. I really don't. My plants are just as important to me as they've always been, and I still care about keeping up with my shows. I try very hard to care about the things that make up my day. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just... giving up on the things I love. That wouldn't be right at all. 

I still care very much. I hope that's an okay answer? I'm so sorry if it's not what you were looking for... I'm really trying to be a good patient for you.
